newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma government still holding top Suu Kyi aide.
newsitem.headline: Burma government still holding top Suu Kyi aide.

text.p: A top official in Aung San Suu Kyi's democracy movement was still being held for questioning on Thursday by Burma's military government for his involvement in a student protest, a senior government official said.

Kyi Maung, deputy chairman of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party and a close adviser to Suu Kyi, was picked up early on Wednesday for his involvement in student protests this week, the official told Reuters.

"He was picked up early on the morning of the 23rd of October and the reason for calling him in for questioning was because...he met with some of the students involved in a protest for over an hour," the official said in an interview.

He did not say where Kyi Maung was being held, nor when he might be released. Kyi Maung, 75, was previously held in Rangoon's infamous Insein Prison from 1990 to 1995 for his role in the democracy movement.
A statement from the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) on Wednesday accused Kyi Maung of colluding with some students involved in a protest on Wednesday morning.
It said he was helping to politicise a scuffle between students and restaurant owners and trying to create unrest by staging a protest.
On Wednesday between 500-1,000 Burmese university students staged a rare demonstration against the military government and its detention of three classmates involved in the scuffle.
Witnesses put the number at about 500 while the government official said it was closer to 1,000.
Human rights organisations and governments condemned the SLORC for Kyi Maung's detention, and called for his immediate release.

"His arrest is an outrage and he should be released immediately," London-based Amnesty International said. "This arrest is part of a relentless attempt by the Myanmar (Burmese) authorities to crush any peaceful dissent by whatever means."
The United States on Wednesday called for Kyi Maung's release and urged the military to start a dialogue with the opposition on the country's future.
Kyi Maung gave speeches to supporters along with Suu Kyi each Sunday at the front gate of the Nobel Peace laureate's Rangoon house.
The government has regularly attacked Kyi Maung through official media, saying he was trying to undermine the peace and stability of the nation.
